lines.en: I don’t believe in silver tongues, nor effervescent light.
Or the songs unmatching eyes doth sing to the choirs of we sodomites.
So pretentious and unwilling — humble vice grip, hold me tight.
It will take more than a color wheel to eradicate this parasite.
Are you lost again? Don’t worry. Dear, that’s how I love you best.
For when you’re safe, you never spend much time on what you keep repressed.
These faded words might not find peace, but they’ll carve into your chest-
And remind you I won’t disappear.
I am simply here to rest.
- “Mommy”
: Sensei?
: Were you having a nightmare? You normally stay really still when you’re asleep, but you were all...tossy and turny just now.
: I’m fine. But thanks for apparently always keeping a close eye on me while I’m passed out. That's not weird at all.
: Of course. What else are nieces for?
: Everything.
: Well, not this one.
: But anyway, now that you’re awake, would you mind explaining to me why there’s a girl here to visit you first thing in the morning?
: Do I really need to explain to you why I’m so popular? Because this is a thing you should probably just know by now.
: Ha ha ha. Yes. Yes, I believe this might be something you will have to explain to me.
: Don’t “ha ha ha” me. Just tell whoever it is that I’ll call them later.
: You most certainly will not. And stop trying to go back to sleep to get away from me.
: Ugh, is it Makoto? Because that pout tells me it’s probably Makoto.
: Are you expecting Makoto?

: I’m never expecting anything...Things just always happen out of nowhere for me and I’m trying to piece together what the actual worst possible scenario is right now since whatever is going on is probably that.
: Yeah, you’re telling me! I didn’t even realize this girl was here for you until she held up a sign! Imagine my surprise when she just walked into the house!
: A...sign?
: Yes! She hasn’t said a single word since she walked in and now she’s wandering around the house inspecting everything!
: Well? What do you have to say about this?
: I’m going back to sleep.
: Knock it off!
: Ami, I don’t know how to handle this situation and any way I explain it is going to sound crazy.

: Well...can you just make her go away then? Because I’ve been trying for like fifteen minutes and she won’t budge. And I don’t know if I like the idea of suspicious children showing up here to hang out with you.
: In fact, I don’t like the idea of anyone showing up here to hang out with you. But this one is particularly weird and even younger than I thought you would have any interest in.
: Okay. Fine. But maybe don’t let strangers into the house anymore if you don’t want them walking around inspecting our stuff.
: Well forgive me for not realizing that was a thing I had to worry about! The heck is going on with this neighborhood nowadays?!
Why?
: Nao, what are you doing here?
: No. This is not a thumbs-up situation.
: Yes, that’s more like it.
So...it appears that the newest character in my life has decided to show up at my door significantly ahead of schedule.
Like...half a decade ahead of schedule. And I have no idea why or how.
: Why? How?
: I have no idea, Ami. I was literally just wondering that.
: Who even is this? I have never seen this girl in my life. Why do you know her name? How are you acquainted with her? Just what exactly have you been doing behind my back?
: It’s a long story.
: Sensei, when you asked me to give you space, I knew you’d use it to make some stupid decisions. But this is not the direction I thought you’d take that in.
: Again, I have no idea why this is happening. Nao shouldn’t even know where I live. And she definitely shouldn’t be wandering around Kumon-mi unsupervised.
: Nao? What’s her family name?
: She doesn’t have one. Well...at least not one anybody knows yet.
: Right...
: And how old is she exactly?
: There’s no way of-
: Oh no.
: For what?!
: Now, before she answers this question, I’d like to make it known that my relationship with Nao can barely even be called a relationship in the first place. She’s more of a-
: You were saying?
: She’s more of some girl that Kaori is looking after that I just happened to get acquainted with through her.
: Oh, okay. That completely explains why she’s asking you to sit on her.
: I think that’s code for babysitting. You need to remember that her mentor is Kaori and that sort of thing can have a negative impact on a young, impressionable girl.
: I know. I wasn’t being sarcastic.
: So...Nao-chan...are you Miss Kaori’s...cousin or something? Because you’re clearly not a niece. I have niece senses and would be able to detect that.
: Well, that doesn’t help at all.
: It’s equally unhelpful that all of her signs appear to be remotely suggestive.
: Well, it’s not like she’s writing them herself. It looks like she’s flipping through the pages to find stuff that was already written down. She might not have an answer to everything.
: Well, we can all be thankful that Kaori decided to include the extremely valuable signs of “old enough” and “25%% off wieners.”
: Stop looking so proud and go find your guardian. I’m not a babysitter.

: Maybe Kaori just felt a little bad since she works all the time? Nao-chan would probably get lonely cooped up in that apartment all by herself. It only makes sense that she’d send her to a friend’s house.
: I should say that I feel a little relieved to find out that this is why you’ve been hanging out with Kaori lately, though. She’s really pretty and I got jealous and...I’m sorry.
: Why are you being so mature? It’s weird.
: This is what you want, isn’t it? If I keep suffocating you-
: PS: Please buy her — wait, why is Kaori putting the “PS” at the top? Isn’t that supposed to go on the bottom?
: Probably the same reason she says goodbye instead of hello- because she’s a lunatic.
: Greetings, Friendburger. I have to cream all day, so please sit on Nao-chan.
: And if she tries to use your mug, don’t let her. She is a mug monster...that means she is like a monster, but with mugs.
: PS: Please buy her new body fabric. I will pay you back with gum.
: Thanks for reading all of that, Ami. My eyes aren’t what they used to be.
: It looks like you’re going to have to take Nao-chan shopping, Sensei.
: What? Why? I wanted to exercise my new freedom and do other stuff today. I shouldn’t be bogged down by babysitting Kaori’s surrogate daughter.
: But think of all the gum you’ll get.
: Ami, can you stay here with Nao for a second while I go call her mother?
: Sure, but if our mugs start disappearing, you’re going to be the one on the hook to buy more. You were warned, Sensei. You know what you’re getting into.
: I think we can live without a few mugs, thanks.
: Good-
: Explain yourself.
: I am Kaori! I came to life when I exited my mothermom and now spend my reverse-nights feeding small creatures to a large creature who-
: No, I mean explain why you sent Nao to my house.
: Nao-chan requires four hours of social interaction each day in order to grow into a healthy bird!
: She is a human.
: Yes, a human bird. What kind of gum do you like?
: Kaori, how did you even get my address? You’ve never been to my house.
: Yes!
: Yes what?
: Address!
I feel like this is going to be a long conversation.
: Okay...Listen up, Nao-chan. I’m going to level with you here.
: Sensei is my uncle and my guardian. And he doesn’t know this yet, but he’s also going to be the father of my children one day and we’re going to raise a beautiful family together.
: Don’t look so disgusted. You shouldn’t even know the real world implications of that yet. And the only reason I’m telling you in the first place is so you don’t try anything funny.
: Sensei is really important to me, okay? And I get that you’re just a little girl who doesn’t really understand how the world works or whatever yet, but...hands off.
: Really? Just like that?
: Huh...Everyone else always puts up a fight.

: Well, I guess you can’t really put up a fight in the first place since you can’t talk. But just know that I’ll be watching you, okay? I don’t fully trust you yet. Especially not after storming into my house.
: You are really cute, though. I’ll give you that much. And you’ve got heterochromia, just like Miss Kaori-
: ...wait a minute.
: Your eyes seem kind of familiar...
: Isn’t that...the same color as mine?
: And isn’t the other one the same color as-
: Hm?
: What? What do you want from me?
: Are you...
: Are you asking me to pat your head?
: Ugh...fine. But if I do this, you have to swear you’ll leave Sensei alone, okay?
: There you go. Is this what you wanted?
: You know, Nao-chan...I think I might be starting to kind of like you! Not being able to talk means you can’t tease me or make fun of me for anything! And people have been doing that a lot lately.
: Do you like me too?
: Yeah, I bet you do. I bet you do.
: Who’s a good girl? Who’s a good girl? Nao-chan’s a good girl, isn’t she? Isn’t she?
: Yeah...you love that, don’t you? Don’t you, Nao-chan?
: How ‘bout there? Is that good too? You want me to rub your ears? Yeah? Yeah?
: Ahem...
: Sensei! It’s not what it looks like!
: I see...so Kaori’s not going to be home until really late and Nao-chan isn’t ready to take care of herself yet.
: Right. And since Yuki’s going to be at the bar all day and Kaori doesn’t have any other friends, I wound up being the next in line.
: Well, what are you gonna do? You can’t just send her off on her own. But you seemed so excited to finally have some Ami-less time for whatever weird reason you actually want Ami-less time.
: Easy. I’m going to make you watch her instead while I go off and be an adult somewhere.
: What?! Why me?!
: Well, to start off, it looked like you two were really getting along just a minute ago.
: That’s only because you won’t let me get a pet and Nao-chan is the closest thing we’ve ever had to that!
: We don’t have Nao. She’s Kaori’s responsibility after today, not ours.
: What if we adopt her?
: What? You wanted her out of the house less than twenty minutes ago. What changed?
: Everything. Everything changed. And now I can’t live without her.
: Can we keep her? Please?
: Ask me again at the end of the day when you’re done babysitting her.
: Sensei, I have work in less than an hour. Not to mention how I’m still on thin ice from the dressing room thingy.
: Just take Nao-chan to the mall or something. That way, you can keep her occupied and find her clothes.
: If all she has is that oversized hoodie, she’s going to overheat. This summer’s been the hottest on record and if Nao-chan dies now, we’ll never get to see how she looks when she’s all grown up.
: It’s really interesting how your heart can be in both the right place and the wrong place at the same time.
: You don’t know the half of it.
: Hah...Nao, do you want to go the mall?
: Wow...Kaori got really specific with these sign choices, didn’t she?
: A mall is like...a big building where you can buy anything you want and...socialize with other people who are there to shop, I guess?
: Well, I guess that settles it then. Don’t have too much fun without me, you two.
: And remember what I told you, Nao-chan...
: Hands off.
: Bye! Time to get ready for work!
: Don’t mind her. She’s broken.
I ask Nao to remain on the couch while I head back into my room to get dressed.
When I return, I notice that all of our cabinets are open and all of our mugs are gone.
Nao’s affection has increased to [nao_love]!
